title: Lumbar puncture in the febrile infant under 60 days
alt: Algorithm: after cultures and inflammatory markers, an unstable infant or one with a contraindication has the LP deferred and antibiotics started. Otherwise an ill-appearing infant, any infant 8 to 21 days, and those 22 to 28 days are tapped; from 29 to 60 days only those with abnormal CRP, procalcitonin or ANC are tapped, and those with normal markers are managed without LP or antibiotics.
caption: Pathway for the well-appearing febrile infant, after the AAP 2021 clinical practice guideline; check local policy.

nodes.text: Febrile infant 60 days or younger: assess appearance, take blood and urine cultures, CRP, procalcitonin, ANC
7 days or younger: full evaluation with LP and admission, however well they look
Unstable, or is there a contraindication to LP?
Shock, respiratory failure, coagulopathy, low platelets, skin infection at the site, signs of raised pressure
Stabilise, give empiric IV antibiotics, defer the LP
Do the LP once stable if age or markers still require it
LP, then empiric IV antibiotics and admission
Perform LP before or with antibiotics: cells, protein, glucose, culture, PCR
Perform LP; stop antibiotics if CSF, markers and cultures are normal
CRP, procalcitonin and ANC all normal?
A positive urine culture with normal markers is a UTI: treat it, no LP needed
No LP, no antibiotics, review within 24 hours
Perform LP and start empiric IV antibiotics
Adjust antibiotics to CSF and cultures; stop all if they are negative
